versions.summary: Renaming a workstream can rename its branch, and PR lookups follow the real branch.
notes: Renaming a workstream can now also rename its app-made branch. The new name is previewed first, and the rename is blocked once the branch is pushed, has a PR, has moved, or the new name is taken.

PR status, merge, base edits and the PR watcher now follow the worktree's actual branch, so a renamed or switched worktree no longer loses its PR. Archive skips deleting the remote branch in that case.
Starting a later stage's session now advances the workstream's stage and never moves it back.
This version works with hyprlayer-server 0.8.18 and later.

versions.summary: The activity bar no longer reports done while background agents are still running.
notes: The activity bar no longer flashes done when a turn ends with background agents or workflows still running; it shows "Waiting for ... to finish" and times the closing turn from the start of the wait.
A subagent permission ask you resolved locally no longer comes back as pending or marks the session as streaming.
This version works with hyprlayer-server 0.8.17 and later.

versions.summary: A status bar shows what the agent is doing, and recaps summarize turns you missed.
notes: A bar above the composer now names what the agent is doing (current tool, waiting on you, or another device working) with elapsed time, and shows the last turn's duration once idle. It replaces the status lines at the bottom of the transcript.
When a turn finishes while you are in another tab, the bar shows a short recap of what it did. Turn this off under Recaps in General settings.
This version works with hyprlayer-server 0.8.17 and later.

versions.summary: Clearer tool rows for searches, fetches and failed commands.
notes: Codex web searches now show as search or fetch rows with their query or URL instead of an empty search.
Failed Codex commands lead with "Exit code N", and grep-style commands that match nothing read "No matches found" instead of an error.
Tool paths in the transcript render relative to the session directory, and Agent and Workflow rows now look like every other tool row.
This version works with hyprlayer-server 0.8.16 and later.

versions.summary: Long shell commands no longer fill the transcript.
notes: Shell commands in the transcript now show at most two lines and 160 characters, as in Claude Code. Expand the row to see the full command.
MCP and other tool calls in the transcript now list all their arguments as key: value pairs, capped at 160 characters, instead of only the first text argument.
This version works with hyprlayer-server 0.8.14 and later.

versions.summary: Tool results summarized in the transcript, and fixes for NVIDIA on Linux and CLI detection.
notes: This version works with hyprlayer-server 0.8.14 and later. Server 0.8.15 adds the CLI detection fix below; a host running an older server is updated once it has been idle for two minutes.
Tool calls in the transcript read as "Name (args)" with a one-line result under them, such as "Found 12 files" for Glob or "… +40 lines" for longer output.
Fixed Hyprlayer crashing a few seconds after launch on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU and WebKitGTK older than 2.54.2.
Onboarding now finds the hyprlayer CLI and other required tools installed after the server started, without restarting the app.

versions.summary: Goals keep agents working until checks pass, with clearer tool calls and context controls.
notes: Start a goal with /goal or the goal button to keep an agent working until its checks pass. Set limits for iterations, active time, and cost or tokens; pause, resume, or stop it from the Goal view. Works with Claude, Codex, and OpenCode.

Plans can now Build until met or Implement until validated, and validation findings offer Fix until met. Check results appear in the transcript and Goal view; plan checks run in the directory the plan names.
Each tool call now has its own row in the main transcript, MCP tools use their server names, and running subagents show their type.
Fixed parallel permission prompts settling the wrong tool call. Allow for session also answers open prompts for that tool, and stopping a session dismisses every pending prompt.
Outdated review notes now stay beside the code, folded like resolved notes. Fixed terminal theme detection for Claude in PTY tabs.

Fixed the context meter still showing the pre-compaction fill after running /compact. It now drops to the size Claude reports for the compacted conversation, which leaves out the system prompt and tools, so the next turn reports a higher figure. Sessions compacted before this fix hide the meter until their next turn.
Fixed the summary from a manual /compact never reaching the compact divider. The divider now expands to show it, as it does after an auto-compact.

Fixed /clear leaving the old fill on the context meter and adding an "unrecognized stream-json line" error to the transcript. The meter now stays hidden until Claude reports the new conversation's size.
Fixed notes Claude adds for itself, such as image size hints, resume nudges after a cut-off reply and hook feedback, showing up in the transcript as its replies.
Clear context, Switch model, Restart session and Delete prompt now ask in an in-app dialog instead of a native alert. Escape or Cancel leaves everything as it was.
Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K now does what the Clear context button does: it asks first while the session is running, then starts fresh. It used to end the session without asking.
When another process holds this profile, Hyprlayer now opens and explains it in the server dialog, with a Relaunch button, instead of showing an alert and quitting.
This version needs hyprlayer-server 0.8.14. Remote hosts on an older server must update before connecting.

versions.summary: Fixes Git LFS checkouts from the Dock and compact summaries leaking into the transcript.
notes: Fixed creating a workstream in a Git LFS repository failing with "git-lfs: command not found" when Hyprlayer was opened from the Dock or Finder. git now gets the same PATH as agents and terminals, so filters, hooks and credential helpers installed with Homebrew are found.
Fixed the summary after a compact showing up as assistant text when Claude put a notice line ahead of it. It now folds into the compact divider.

versions.summary: Fixes the plan view tracking the wrong phase.
notes: Fixed the plan view tracking the wrong phase when an earlier phase had a deferred check. The current phase is now the first unfinished one after the last phase with progress, and sub-phases like 7B resolve to their parent.
The plan phase line shows the plan's own label when it differs from the position (Phase 5b · 6 of 9), and the current phase leads the remaining list.

versions.summary: Update an outdated server from the status bar; plan and PR record statuses stay current.
notes: This version needs hyprlayer-server 0.8.11. A host running an older server is updated once it has been idle for two minutes; turn off "Update server when idle" in Settings to update it yourself.
The status bar shows an Update server button when the connected server is outdated, and runs the update in place with a progress label instead of the disconnected dialog.
The local server now also updates shortly after launch when nothing has been touched yet. Remote hosts still wait for the idle window.
Plan and PR record statuses now follow the workstream, session, and PR state, so they no longer go stale.

versions.summary: Fixes git detection and skills.sh skill previews on Windows.
notes: Fixed git and gh showing as missing on Windows when installed only on the system PATH (for example C:\Program Files\Git\cmd).
Fixed skills.sh skill details failing with "Couldn't reach the skill source" on Windows.

versions.summary: Messages you send mid-turn queue instead of steering; review and validation get clearer panels.
notes: Enter on a message sent mid-turn now queues it to run after the turn, instead of steering the agent. Use Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to steer. Stop pulls queued messages back into the composer.
Queued messages show inline at the end of the transcript instead of in a strip above the composer.
Fixed streamed text breaking mid-sentence for a reader that attached partway through a turn.
Validate and review now show as ordered steps in the plan sidebar and chat card. Validation findings split into gate, checks, issues, notes, and manual items, with a fix-or-skip choice.
Review notes drop the "needs your call" kind; the review panel counts unresolved notes instead.
Keyboard focus reads like hover instead of drawing a ring, and arrow keys navigate lists.

versions.summary: Sign in to ssh hosts that need a password, passphrase or new host key.
notes: Remote hosts that need an ssh password, key passphrase, one-time code, or trust in a new host key now ask in an in-app dialog instead of failing or hanging. Nothing is stored.
You're asked once per host, not on every connect or install step.
A changed host key is never offered for trust; the error shows the ssh-keygen -R command to run instead.
Cancelling a sign-in stops the reconnect attempts, and a failed host's button reads "Sign in" when a prompt can fix it.
On Windows, ssh sign-in is unchanged.

versions.summary: Fixes adding a Mac host with no server installed, and collapsed text areas.
notes: Fixed the host connection test failing on a Mac with no server installed, so a fresh Mac can now be added as a host.
Fixed a text area collapsing to zero height when it was measured before being attached to the page, as in editor widgets.

versions.summary: Sign in with GitHub, switch permission modes mid-turn, and navigate library lists by keyboard.
notes: This version needs hyprlayer-server 0.8.9. A host running an older server is updated once it has been idle for two minutes; turn off "Update server when idle" in Settings to update it yourself.
Sign in to Hyprlayer Cloud with GitHub from the account button in the top bar.
Changing a Claude session's permission mode no longer restarts it or interrupts the running turn.
Cmd/Ctrl + Enter stops the running turn and sends your message right away, with a hint beside the stop button. The "Request interrupted by user" notice is hidden.
Library lists respond to Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home, and End, and the detail pane follows the selection without flashing.
Library mailbox counts now match the list each one opens when filters are applied.
Thoughts sync is hidden for projects without thoughts set up, and sync failures show in a hover card.

versions.summary: Install and manage skills, open existing worktrees, and update idle servers automatically.
notes: This version needs hyprlayer-server 0.8.8. A host running an older server is updated once it has been idle for two minutes; turn off "Update server when idle" in Settings to update it yourself.

Workshop is the home for agents, skills, and prompts. Install a skill from a GitHub link or skills.sh, browse skills.sh leaderboards, and update, restore, or remove installed skills. Skills can include scripts or executables, and the app warns before installing them.
The skill detail view shows bundled files and opens the skill folder in your editor.
Open a git worktree created outside the app as a workstream.
Library is a three-pane view with excerpts, read state that syncs across devices, and the agent that wrote each doc.
The code review workspace diffs a workstream against its base branch. Reply to an agent's review note to answer it.
The project pipeline is the project view, with board, table, and triage layouts.
Plan panel: finished phases fold into a Completed section, and a phase with a running foreman shows as building.
Removed decorative UI, including placeholder dashboard stats and glow animations.
App zoom now steps 1.2× per level, up to level 8. Stored zoom values snap to the nearest step.
Fixed one unreadable message dropping the server connection and every session on it.

versions.summary: Sessions sync across devices, with new appearance controls and a cleaner workspace.
notes: When another device adds turns to a session you have open, they wait until you click Load, so they never stream in or play alert sounds while you work; sending with turns waiting asks you to load them first so your message answers the latest state, and your draft stays.
While another device's turn runs, a "<device> is working…" placeholder shows in place of its live output; its messages appear when you load them.
The server now refuses a message sent from an out-of-date transcript instead of running it; a queued message that is refused waits for the pull and is sent after it.
A message sent while another device's turn is running waits for that turn to finish.
Sessions show which devices are viewing them.

Appearance settings now include app zoom, four text sizes, interface and code font choices, and terminal font size. Use Cmd/Ctrl + plus, minus, or zero for app zoom; add Shift to change terminal font size.
Settings and your profile moved to the top bar, archived worktrees are in Settings, and the status bar sits below the agent view. The workstream breadcrumb shows its agent tab count.
Dialogs, menus, and buttons have smoother transitions that respect reduced-motion preferences.
Fixed a terminal error when closing a terminal while a scroll update was pending.
Transcript sync needs hyprlayer-server 0.8.6; with an older server, a notice offers to load new turns instead.

versions.summary: A plan view beside every agent, sessions shared across devices, and a new status bar.
notes: Plans now open in an aside next to the agent: phase-by-phase progress, plan cards in the transcript, and Approve & build to hand off to implementation. Works with Claude, Codex, and OpenCode plans.
Agent sessions, titles, and archives now live on the server, so every connected device sees the same list. The sessions popover has an Archived view (⌘⇧A) with Archive and Delete.
Settings moved into a popover, and a new status bar shows plan mode, switches servers, and holds archived worktrees.
Archived worktrees are kept for 30 days, with Keep, Purge, and restore to a different location.
Library docs render as markdown and switch to editing on click, with a properties rail for frontmatter fields and related-doc links.
Dark mode moves to a new grayscale palette, alongside a refreshed type scale.
Stopping a working agent now asks first. Session titles generate faster and retry once on failure.
Fixed launch hanging on an asleep remote host; it now fails within 15 seconds.
Fixed sessions left mid-turn by a server restart still looking live, with permission prompts that could never resolve.
Fixed plan-mode progress showing 0% for phase-only plans and tasks from an earlier plan carrying into a new one.
This version needs hyprlayer-server 0.8.5. Hosts on an older server show an "Update server" action.

versions.summary: Fixed a slow server start-up race and a stale-connection hang; test suite cleanup.
notes: Fixed a race where a slow server start (a fresh profile's first migration, or a debug build) could be mistaken for a failure to connect.
Fixed a stale connection lingering after a server restarted instead of closing right away.
Setting up thoughts with a relative path is now rejected with a clear error instead of silently writing to the wrong place.

versions.summary: The server now updates independently of the app; codex support raised to 0.155.1.
notes: Updating Hyprlayer no longer restarts a running server (and drops its sessions) unless the update actually needs a newer one. A host running an old server now offers an "Update server" action instead of just flagging the problem.
Raised the supported codex-cli version to 0.155.1. Rewind now works on newer codex threads, and codex sessions turn on the built-in planning tool.
Codex sessions always start with project memory as reference notes now, instead of only on certain versions.

versions.summary: Fixed OpenCode keys on remote hosts; added a Copy Diagnostics / Reveal Logs menu.
notes: Fixed a bug where adding or changing an OpenCode API key in Settings didn't reach a remote host running your session; keys now update on the server that needs them.
Help > Copy Diagnostics and Reveal Logs make it easy to grab logs when something goes wrong, with secrets like API keys automatically redacted.
A crash while rendering one page no longer takes down the whole window; it now shows an error in place with a Reveal Logs action.

versions.summary: Composer controls move below the input; host status shows on its own row.
notes: The composer's agent mode, model, reasoning effort and permission pickers now sit in a row below the input box instead of inside it.

Installing or restarting a server in the Hyprlayer server dialog now shows its progress on that host's row, including "Restarting…" while a restart is in flight, so it's clear which host is doing the work.
The server-disconnected notice now closes on its own once the server reconnects, instead of staying up until you relaunch.

versions.summary: Sessions keep running after you quit, remote hosts over SSH, and split panes.
notes: Sessions, terminals and scripts now keep running when you quit Hyprlayer. The app's backend moved into a background process, hyprlayer-server, which the app starts on launch and reconnects to when reopened: a session mid-turn keeps streaming and terminals reattach. It ships inside the app. To stop it, run `hyprlayer-server stop`; the binary sits next to the Hyprlayer executable (Hyprlayer.app/Contents/MacOS on macOS, /usr/bin on Linux).

Updating works differently from here on. After an update, the server the previous version started keeps your sessions running, and the globe icon in the left rail shows a warning until you choose Restart server in its dialog, which ends every running session and terminal. An update that changes how the app and server talk replaces the old server on launch instead, ending them too. This update has no server to replace. To go back to 0.7, run `hyprlayer-server stop` first.

Hyprlayer can run sessions on another machine over SSH. Add the host in the Hyprlayer server dialog (the globe icon) using any destination ssh accepts, and the app offers to install a matching server there. Supported hosts are Apple Silicon Macs and x86_64 Linux with glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40). Folder pickers browse the host, and a dropped connection reconnects on its own. git on the host uses that machine's credentials.

The server is also packaged on its own, for a machine you leave running: `paru -S hyprlayer-server-bin` on Arch, `brew install brightblock/tap/hyprlayer-server` on macOS and Linuxbrew. Installing starts nothing; run `hyprlayer-server serve`, or enable the systemd unit (Arch) or launchd agent (macOS) it ships. On Arch it conflicts with the desktop package, which already contains the server.

Sessions split into any number of panes, side by side or stacked. Split right with Cmd+\ or down with Cmd+Shift+\, or drag a tab onto a pane's edge, and move between panes with Cmd+Option+arrow keys (Ctrl and Alt on Windows and Linux). Each pane has its own tabs and can be resized, closed or maximized. Existing two-pane layouts carry over, and unsaved edits in a file tab survive switching away.

Claude Code's project memory is visible from the workstream panel: the lightbulb button lists the repository's memory files, MEMORY.md first, and opens them for viewing and editing. A save is refused if the file changed on disk since you started editing. Codex tabs on codex-cli 0.152.0 or newer start with the memory index as reference notes, unless you set your own developer instructions.
The context-window meter now reads the window size claude reports each turn, so Hyprlayer no longer reads your Claude login from the macOS Keychain.
Tab and document changes made in the second before an update or relaunch are no longer lost.

versions.summary: Model pickers show the live Claude catalog, with reasons for unavailable models.
notes: The Claude model pickers now show what your installed CLI actually supports, merged from a live probe instead of a fixed list. The entry that follows the CLI's own default is labeled "Default", with the model it currently resolves to shown in the hint beneath it — so you can see what you'll actually get rather than having to guess which one "default" means today.

Models your setup can't use are now listed with the reason they're unavailable, instead of being hidden outright. That covers both the agent editor's model rows and the composer's model menu, where a missing model previously just wasn't there, with nothing to explain why.
Updating the Claude CLI now refreshes that catalog on its own, rather than leaving a stale list behind until the next restart.

versions.summary: Memory fixes: terminal buffers freed, orphaned OpenCode servers reaped, output backpressured.
notes: Switching agent tabs or workstreams no longer leaves the old terminal's scrollback sitting in memory. The channel feeding a terminal outlives the view that shows it, so a closed terminal stayed reachable and kept filling a buffer nobody could see — roughly 9–15 MB per terminal once its 5,000-line scrollback filled up. Closing a terminal now releases the buffer, and writes to one that's already closed are dropped rather than accumulated.

An OpenCode server orphaned by a crash or a force-quit is now cleaned up on the next launch. Quitting normally always shut the server down, but a crash skipped that path and left `opencode serve` running indefinitely — three strays measured on one machine came to about 700 MB combined, alive for six to nine hours. The app now records its server and reaps it at startup, first confirming the live process still matches what it recorded so an unrelated process that reused the same pid is never touched.

A command that floods its output no longer grows an unbounded backlog in the background. Terminal output is capped at about 128 KB in flight, which lets the pty push back on the program the same way a real terminal would.

That orphan cleanup now also works on mise-managed installs and on macOS. It had identified the server by the exact path it launched, which never matches once a mise shim re-execs the real binary — so on those setups every orphan was skipped as an unrelated process. It now matches on the binary name and the port being served, so a plain `opencode` session, or a server on a different port, is still left alone.

Jumping to a background task from the transcript now works when its group is collapsed. The jump used to scroll straight to the tool's own row, which doesn't exist yet if the group around it is closed, so the view landed somewhere arbitrary — the group now opens first and the scroll follows it. Bottom-pinning is also suspended while a jump is in flight, so the transcript stops dragging you back down mid-scroll.

versions.summary: Create new projects from the app, plus a fix for stuck working indicators.
notes: Add Project can now create a brand-new project instead of only importing or cloning one. It makes the folder, runs git init on the branch name you pick, puts a README and .gitignore in the first commit, and can publish straight to GitHub in the same pass with an owner/organization picker and live per-step progress. If only the GitHub step fails the project is still usable locally, and you can correct a rejected name or owner and retry just that step rather than starting over.

Fixed a session that could sit on "working…" forever. A background agent's events kept arriving after its parent turn had already finished, and each one re-flagged the session as still streaming. Background agent and subagent tasks now track their own open state, so their spinners stop when the task actually stops.

The repair for a workstream's broken thoughts links is reachable again — it's an item in the workstream's right-click menu, shown only when the links are genuinely broken. It now refuses outright when the worktree itself is missing, instead of recreating it as an empty shell that would block recovering the workstream properly.

Settings → Binaries now flags a Codex older than 0.149, which is what the Codex features added in 0.7.2 actually need. Before this, a too-old Codex reported healthy and then failed when a session tried to start.

Internal: the Rust backend is reorganized behind a runtime library boundary — shared contracts, a core engine, and a thin desktop shell. No behavior change is intended; your settings, database and stored session history carry over untouched, pinned by new compatibility tests against the previous release's on-disk formats.

versions.summary: Codex gains Claude skills, agents, and question cards; agent settings repair flow.
notes: Codex sessions can now use your .claude/skills library, which only the Claude harness could see before. The composer's slash menu is harness-aware too: a Codex session lists skills under codex's own $name sigil and drops the Claude-only prompt expansions it can't run.

Codex now asks through the same structured question card Claude uses instead of asking in prose. Commit, Plan and Research run as two turns there — the first reviews or explores and asks its questions, the second carries the work out with your answers. Commit asks whether to push before it commits anything, so answering no means no push is ever attempted.
Fixed layout flicker when resizing panes: the animated sidebar width transitions are gone, and the transcript stays pinned to the bottom through a resize instead of drifting.
The Hyprlayer and AI Agents settings cards are now one card, with a one-click Repair that reinstalls the agent bundle directly instead of handing you a terminal dialog.

Repair now clears what was blocking it. A stale or hand-edited file sitting on a bundle's target path used to leave the relink permanently stuck; identical copies are now deleted, modified ones are backed up alongside as .bak files, and the receipt showing which is which stays on screen.

A CLI that reports only one of the Claude/Codex agent pair gets its own Unpaired state rather than being folded in with a pre-1.6.0 CLI, the CLI update button is always available, and the app no longer nags you to update a CLI that's already current.

Fixed the tab-title model staying on the outgoing harness's default after you switch your default harness, and OpenCode's model list is now reconciled against the running server so models it no longer offers can't be selected.

versions.summary: Fixed the AI Agents bundle status going stale after a CLI upgrade.
notes: Upgrading the hyprlayer CLI and hitting Re-detect used to leave the agent bundle showing the old version until an app restart — the bundle's own status now refreshes along with everything else a CLI upgrade affects.

Bundle freshness is more accurate now too: instead of a signal that just says "has the CLI's repo moved", it directly compares your installed version against the current one, and a legacy CLI whose bundle can no longer receive new skills is now flagged distinctly rather than shown as plain "Up to date".
Settings can now offer and run a hyprlayer CLI update directly from the frozen-bundle notice, instead of just telling you to go update it yourself.
The AI Agents card is now a subsection of the Hyprlayer card instead of a separate card, since they're driven by the same CLI.

versions.summary: Omarchy theme support, Workflow subagent visibility, and Linux fixes.
notes: Added an Omarchy theme to match that desktop environment's palette.
Workflow subagent activity (parallel agents spawned during a multi-step task) now surfaces properly in the transcript instead of being invisible.
Fixed pinch-to-zoom on Linux accidentally zooming the whole app instead of the page content — the webview now ignores that gesture.
Fixed a Linux transcript click bug and cut down its rendering/persistence overhead.
The Settings reinstall flow now keeps its backup if a reinstall fails instead of discarding it, and the version picker is tighter.

versions.summary: Agents get folder management + a publish toggle; fixed doc misattribution.
notes: The Agents sidebar now supports folder management — right-click to create an agent in a folder or delete an empty one — plus a publish/unpublish toggle instead of a one-way Publish action, and a Default badge showing which agent is the library's default.

System-raised confirm dialogs (like quitting via the dock) now auto-focus their confirm button, and several dialog/menu sizing bugs are fixed — a narrow popover opening at the wrong width, and dialogs stuck at a fixed width regardless of what they asked for.
A workstream could pick up a doc it only read — never wrote — as one of its own written docs, if another workstream had actually written it. Attribution is now scoped correctly per workstream.

versions.summary: New Agents view, Commits tab, and Settings panel; Linux tiling WM support.
notes: A new Agents view manages your .claude/agents/*.md files directly in the app — browse the library, edit frontmatter and body, pick which skills preload, and set per-agent launch settings that the markdown itself has nowhere to store.

The Agents view now also tells you when your installed agent bundle is behind BrightBlock/hyprlayer-cli, with one-click update and restore-from-backup, so you can see you are stale without having to reinstall to find out.

A new Commits tab in the right sidebar lists every commit a workstream has ahead of its base branch, with per-commit file diffs — including renames — so you can review what a branch actually did without leaving the app.
Settings moved into its own sidebar panel instead of sharing the Library surface, and Library, Prompts, and Settings now all open at the same width.

Linux: the app now works under tiling window managers like Hyprland and sway. The window can shrink to 500x400 and the shell degrades into a narrow layout tier — project and diff panels become overlay drawers, and resize grips return now that the OS chrome is gone at small sizes. Window dragging also no longer fires on a plain click.

In-place workstreams now follow the branch you are actually on. A `git checkout` run outside the app used to leave the row pinned to a stale branch, which meant wrong PR lookups and wrong base comparisons; the app now adopts the live branch, flags an in-place checkout that has branched away from its base, and shows "detached HEAD" during a rebase instead of stale state.
Ship no longer misfires into an unrelated code-review skill mid-run — it runs as a scoped inline agent, so it does the one job it was asked to do.
Plan, research, and handoff docs are now detected when an agent writes them through Bash rather than the file tools, and no longer show up twice when a worktree is reached through a symlinked path.
claude.ai artifacts published during a session are surfaced in the Changes panel, deduped across a workstream, and open the hosted page on click.
Faster search indexing (lazy body reads plus aho-corasick matching), and syntax highlighting now loads a curated per-language grammar bundle instead of the full set.

versions.summary: Fixed idle CPU burn from filesystem watching and background animations.
notes: On Linux, the app could sit at ~34% of a core doing nothing — a git-status read was mistaken for a file change and kept re-triggering itself. Filesystem watching is also far lighter now: one real worktree went from 4052 armed watches down to 60.
Decorative animations (like the dashboard's pulse ring) now pause while the window isn't focused instead of rendering off-screen — an unfocused window dropped from 8.5% to under 1% of a core.

versions.summary: Fixed Ship going stale from spent GitHub quota; PR docs auto-close on merge.
notes: The Ship button could go stale and show no PR when one existed — background PR polling now only runs at full speed for the workstream you're actually viewing, so idle branches stop burning through GitHub's hourly GraphQL quota.
A workstream's PR description doc now flips to "implemented" automatically once its PR merges, instead of staying open forever.
The nav rail's active item is now marked with an edge accent bar instead of a filled icon, matching VS Code's activity-bar convention, with a bit more breathing room between icons.

versions.summary: Fixed the 0.5.8 Linux packages breaking hyprlayer, git, and gh detection.
notes: Installing the 0.5.8 deb/rpm/AUR package to /usr/bin made a dev-build safety guard blacklist the entire system bin directory, so the app could no longer find the hyprlayer CLI, shell out to git, or read gh's logged-in account correctly. All three now resolve again.

versions.summary: Linux now ships as an AUR/deb/rpm package instead of an AppImage.
notes: Linux installs now come from a proper distro package — the AUR (Arch), a .deb (Debian/Ubuntu), or a .rpm (Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE) — instead of a self-updating AppImage.
Because your package manager now owns installs and updates, the app no longer self-updates on Linux — it points you at `paru`/`apt`/`dnf` instead when a new version is out.
If you're on the 0.5.6 or 0.5.7 AppImage: it won't offer this update. Grab the AUR/deb/rpm package once and your package manager takes it from there.

versions.summary: Linux fixes: clean process env, clipboard image paste, and bundled fonts.
notes: Terminals and harness CLIs (claude, codex, opencode) launched from the Linux AppImage no longer inherit its bundled runtime environment — the worst case broke every `python` invocation with a missing-stdlib error.
Pasting a screenshot into the composer now works on Linux — WebKitGTK's clipboard paste never carried image bytes, so it now falls back to reading the OS clipboard directly.
The UI now bundles Inter and JetBrains Mono instead of relying on the system font stack, fixing missing font weights and a non-monospaced code font on typical Linux installs.

versions.summary: Hyprlayer now ships for Linux, with in-app dropdowns and smarter branch picking.
notes: Hyprlayer is now available on Linux (x64) as an AppImage, alongside macOS and Windows — the same in-app Update pill keeps it current.
Every dropdown and select is now drawn in-app instead of as an OS popup, fixing white GTK menus on Linux and inconsistent sizing on every platform.
New workstreams can now adopt a branch that only exists on the remote — a colleague's pushed work, or a branch from another machine — instead of hiding it from the picker.

versions.summary: Custom prompts can now take {{input}} arguments via /slug.
notes: Custom prompts can define {{input}} / {{input:label}} slots filled at run time — typing a prompt's /slug in the composer holds the send until the argument is typed, instead of baking a fixed body.
The composer's autocomplete now offers prompt slugs alongside claude's real commands, deferring to a real command on name collision.

versions.summary: Plain local folders as projects, and a live Claude model catalog.
notes: Plain local folders can now be added as projects, without needing to be a git repo — git, PR, and thoughts features stay hidden for these.
The model picker now syncs live from the claude CLI's own model list, so new models show up automatically and org-disabled models are clearly marked instead of silently failing.
Fixed item rows in the sidebar being misaligned with their project header.

versions.summary: Stop mislabeling app-initiated kills as "Session ended".
notes: Quitting, archiving, or relaunching a session no longer stamps "Session ended" across every transcript on next launch — the app can now tear a process down for its own bookkeeping without marking the session as user-ended.
On macOS, sessions stopped by a signal (like Ctrl-C) now correctly show as killed instead of crashed.

versions.summary: Stop false crash reports and orphaned processes on quit.
notes: Sessions terminated by an app quit or restart no longer show as "Session crashed" on Windows.
Fixed Codex/OpenCode tabs getting stuck behind a phantom turn after resuming a restarted app.
Agent and OpenCode processes are now killed on app exit instead of occasionally outliving the app for days.
New thoughts repo roots created from onboarding or profile creation are now scaffolded so the CLI accepts them immediately, instead of only while empty.

versions.summary: Codex follow-up fixes: model picker, network access, faster launch.
notes: Codex models now show up in the picker from any tab, not just once you're already on Codex, and default to offering every probed model until you curate a subset.
Fixed Codex's workspace-write sandbox blocking network access even after a command was approved.
Stage sessions now launch in the background so the UI paints immediately instead of blocking on the Codex handshake.

versions.summary: Native Codex harness support, and a confirm-before-quit setting.
notes: Codex is now a first-class harness alongside Claude and OpenCode, with its own model picker, API-key sign-in, and live reasoning-effort switching mid-chat.
Quitting the app (⌘Q, Quit menu, or the window close button) now asks for confirmation by default, since it kills every running agent, PTY, and lifecycle script. Turn it off in Settings > General.

Fixed a handful of Windows-only process bugs affecting Codex and OpenCode: process spawning, orphaned server processes on quit, and startup races that could make a signed-in Codex account look signed out.
The transcript no longer misreports certain internal Claude protocol lines as errors, and re-pins its scroll position correctly when the window resizes.

versions.summary: Fix CLI detection on Windows falsely reporting itself installed.
notes: On Windows, the hyprlayer CLI check no longer mistakes the desktop app's own exe (answering via a winget portable shim) for a real CLI install.

versions.summary: Liquid glass on the sidebar and tabs, collapsible project trees.
notes: The Projects sidebar and tab strip now use the same liquid-glass blur treatment as the rest of the window on macOS.
Each project's workstream list can now be collapsed under a disclosure chevron, VSCode-explorer style.
The header breadcrumb no longer slides sideways when the sidebar resizes or collapses.

versions.summary: Clearer transcript markers for queued commands and wakeups.
notes: Queued slash commands and scheduled wakeups now render a clear seam marking a new turn, instead of looking like the agent spontaneously resumed or showing raw "unrecognized stream-json line" error cards.

versions.summary: Map new projects into named thoughts profiles.
notes: The Add-project dialog's Thoughts step can now target a named thoughts profile, including creating one inline, instead of always mapping under the default.
Picking a repo from Discover now routes through the same Add-project wizard as a pasted URL, so both get the same location and thoughts-mapping steps.
Profile creation now goes through the CLI instead of a raw config edit, keeping the app's config in sync with the CLI's own schema.

versions.summary: Surface Full Disk Access status instead of failing silently.
notes: The app now detects missing Full Disk Access and shows a dismissible notice pointing at the settings pane, instead of gated reads failing silently or a confusing "access data from other apps" dialog.

versions.summary: Safari-style tab closing, merge menu fix, smarter repo sorting.
notes: ⌘W now archives the focused agent tab instead of ending it, with ⌘⇧T to reopen; ⌘⇧W still closes for good. ⌘1–⌘9 jump to tabs directly.
Fixed the merge menu getting clipped by the sidebar instead of floating over the main pane.
The Discover dialog now groups your GitHub repos by owner and sorts recent repos by actual push time.

versions.summary: Collapsible prompt cards, script Clear button, wider diff sidebar.
notes: Turns started from a library prompt now collapse into a compact, expandable card in the transcript instead of showing the full prompt body.
Added a Clear button to the script dock that wipes captured output, including live scrollback.
Widened the right diff sidebar's default and minimum width for more room.
Fixed the app icon mark to match the in-app brand color and proportions.
Fixed script spawn errors showing "[object Object]" instead of the actual error message.

versions.summary: Simpler project import, dashboard and theme fixes.
notes: Adding a project now offers to git-init a plain folder on the spot instead of failing with a bare error, and correctly handles bare/unborn repos.
The dashboard's knowledge graph now shows up as soon as thoughts setup is finished, even before you've added a repo.
New users now default to the system theme instead of the Claude palette.

versions.summary: Editable file viewer with save, and cleaner word-level diffs.
notes: The file viewer is now editable: save with File > Save or Cmd+S, with markdown rendering alongside editing.
Diffs now highlight only the words that actually changed within a modified line, instead of tinting the whole line.
Added a keybinding to toggle markdown preview.

versions.summary: Squared-off panel toggle icons and aligned OpenIn button.
notes: Redrew the panel toggle icons as a symmetric square to match the editor icon's weight, and fixed the OpenIn button to align with its sibling header icons.

versions.summary: Drag-to-reorder projects and reliable rewind across resumes.
notes: Projects in the sidebar can now be reordered by dragging.
Fixed session rewind when using --resume: UUIDs are now read directly from Claude's on-disk transcript so rewind works correctly across resumed sessions.

versions.summary: Nested untracked files now list individually in the changes panel.
notes: The changes panel now recurses into untracked directories so nested files appear as individual entries instead of a collapsed folder.

versions.summary: PR review gate on Merge, smarter watcher, and context-attach fix.
notes: The Merge button is now gated on a typed review decision — approved reviews are required before merging.
The file watcher now detects git changes in worktrees that fall outside the tracked directory tree.
Context attachment is unified into the composer for all turns, not just the first.

versions.summary: Run-script output persists after the script exits.
notes: Output from run scripts is now preserved in the session after the script finishes, so you can review it after exit.

versions.summary: Transcript memory released on tab close and archive.
notes: In-memory transcripts are now released when a tab is closed or archived, reducing memory usage in long sessions.

versions.summary: Sidebar tasks, auto-growing composer, and IA enforcement refactor.
notes: Plan tasks now live in the project sidebar instead of the composer drawer, keeping session writing space focused.
The composer textarea now starts at one row and grows up to 320px as prompts get longer.
IA vocabulary and frontend layering enforcement moved into shared domain/core boundaries with typed enums and updated rules.

versions.summary: Observatory home view, Ship gating, and rewind memory fix.
notes: The home screen is now an Observatory view with an activity graph, live agent list, and a first-run state.
Ship is now gated on the branch being ahead of base, so the button hides correctly after a push.
Fixed rewind so memory is truly truncated and ordinal mapping stays correct across resumes.

versions.summary: Prompt library with ⌘K palette and import/export.
notes: A new prompt library lets you save and reuse prompts, accessible via a ⌘K palette from anywhere in the app.
Prompt bundles can now be exported and imported to share libraries between installations.
Semantic icons replace SparkleIcon across the UI for clearer affordances.

versions.summary: Configurable default harness, Commit/Ship model, and Library state restore.
notes: You can now set a default harness and a separate model for Commit and Ship actions in Settings.
The Library resumes where you left off — same doc, scroll position, and panel state — when you re-enter it.

versions.summary: Library auto-syncs the thoughts repo on open.
notes: Opening the Library now automatically pulls the latest changes from the thoughts repo so your docs are always up to date.

versions.summary: Wide layout for maximized big-display windows.
notes: The dashboard now uses a wide layout when the window is maximized on large displays.

versions.summary: Home screen rebuilt as an operational fleet overview.
notes: The home screen is now a live fleet overview showing all active and recent agent sessions at a glance.

versions.summary: Live context meter, onboarding fix, and Windows update.
notes: The context meter now sizes itself from the live Anthropic Models API so it reflects each model's real window.
Fixed the transcript pin dropping on non-scroll-wheel events (e.g. trackpad momentum).
Onboarding now repoints an existing thoughts config instead of dead-ending the wizard.
Resolved a winget identity collision between the desktop app and the CLI on Windows.

versions.summary: Plan drawer spacing fix and window size restored correctly on reopen.
notes: The plan drawer now has breathing room below composer banners so content isn't clipped.
Fixed window reopening at the wrong size across DPI and monitor changes.

versions.summary: Ultracode effort preset and live model switching for Claude sessions.
notes: A new Ultracode effort preset is available for Claude sessions.
Model switching now takes effect live mid-session without restarting.

versions.summary: Script dock backgrounds themed with surface token.
notes: The script dock, editor, and output panel backgrounds now use the surface theme token, blending cleanly with the rest of the UI.

versions.summary: Per-tab identity and reliable session resume for multiplexer agents.
notes: Each multiplexer agent tab now carries its own conversation identity, and session resume is gated authoritatively so agents never resume into the wrong session.

versions.summary: Multiplexer mode: agents run in persistent PTYs.
notes: Multiplexer mode runs agent CLIs in persistent PTYs so sessions survive reconnects and tab switches.
The plan drawer now remembers its view state (collapsed/expanded sections) across tab-switch remounts.
Cursor blink is disabled for Codex agent tabs.

versions.summary: Scripts dock layout persists and keyboard shortcuts rewired.
notes: The scripts dock now remembers its layout between sessions.
⌘` and ⌘⇧F shortcuts have been rewired for the scripts dock.

versions.summary: Project lifecycle scripts: Setup, Run, and Archive.
notes: Projects now support Setup, Run, and Archive scripts that can be configured and run directly from the app.

versions.summary: File and diff preview now renders correctly in release builds.
notes: Fixed a CSP issue in release builds that caused the file and diff preview to render unstyled.

versions.summary: VSCode-style frameless window on Windows and Linux.
notes: Windows and Linux now use a frameless window with a custom title bar, matching the macOS look.

versions.summary: Agent archive, real context meter, smoother animations.
notes: Sessions can now be archived directly from the agent view.
The context meter now reflects the model's actual context window size rather than a fixed estimate.
Sidebar and panel slide animations respect the system reduced-motion setting.

versions.summary: Sticky update toast and cleaner task lifecycle.
notes: The update pill in the sidebar is replaced by a sticky action toast that appears when an update is ready.
Tasks deleted via TaskUpdate with status "deleted" are now correctly removed from the session.

versions.summary: Transcript stays pinned when the composer resizes.
notes: Fixed the transcript jumping away from the bottom when the composer grows or shrinks (e.g. while typing a long prompt or after a reply lands).

versions.summary: Stability and polish improvements.
notes: Minor stability improvements and internal updates.

versions.summary: CLI install step in onboarding and Windows update card.
notes: Onboarding now includes a CLI install step so the hyprlayer CLI is set up as part of first-run.
The manual update check card is now shown on Windows only, where auto-update is unavailable.

versions.summary: macOS app menu shortcuts and settings redesign.
notes: Added Check for Updates and Settings (Cmd+,) to the macOS app menu. Checking for updates shows a toast with the result; Settings navigates directly.

Redesigned the Hyprlayer config card with an inline backend badge, a Found/Missing indicator, and a click-to-copy config path. Tightened settings copy throughout and removed the redundant updates card from General.

versions.summary: OpenCode transcript fixes and a session-locked model picker.
notes: Fixed OpenCode reasoning leaking into the chat: pre-role reasoning, late-arriving text after a tool call (which could append a duplicate), and inline <think> tags from some free models now render as proper thinking blocks instead of prose.

The model picker now locks to a started session's provider, greying out cross-provider rows. Switching mid-session to a stricter provider could replay the tool history to a new endpoint and hard-fail the turn.

versions.summary: Ollama harness, auto-named agent tabs, and a dedicated workstream GIT panel.
notes: Run your agents on local or remote Ollama models. Settings → Harnesses → Ollama probes any reachable server for its installed models and exposes them in the composer picker.

New agent tabs now auto-title from a summary of your first prompt with a small model (configurable in Settings → General). The title types out in the tab strip and locks once set — a manual rename is never overwritten.

A new GIT panel in the changes sidebar collects per-workstream git controls: an ahead/behind chip, base-branch retargeting that re-points an already-open PR, pull-base (fetch + merge), and a prune-fetch refresh. Archiving a merged workstream can now also delete its remote branch when you've opted in.

versions.summary: Scrollable tabs and OpenCode stability fixes.
notes: The tab strip is now scrollable: when tabs overflow, edge chevrons appear so you can scroll left and right without losing any open session.
Fixed live OpenCode model switching, auth token refresh, and Claude session resume and permission-mode handling so backend state stays consistent across reconfigurations.

versions.summary: OpenCode as an alternative agent backend, plus a re-runnable Commit action and a background-task fix.
notes: Run your agents on OpenCode as an alternative to the Claude CLI. A new Settings → Harnesses section configures each backend — model and provider pickers with per-provider API keys — and the session composer gains a harness and model picker. OpenCode Zen's free models work without a key.
The header Commit action now re-runs: clicking it again after making more changes sends a follow-up /commit turn to the still-live commit tab, instead of just re-selecting it.
Fixed phantom background tasks that could linger as “running” forever after the owning process died on an app restart, resume, rewind, or session exit.

versions.summary: A redesigned sidebar nav rail and unified Library, plus light-theme polish and session-recovery fixes.
notes: The left sidebar is rebuilt around a fixed activity-bar nav rail that stays visible at all times — Home, Projects, and Library up top, with Archive, Settings, and the update pill at the foot. The Projects button now toggles the project panel VS Code-style, the project panel and the diff sidebar glide open and closed instead of snapping, and project and workstream rows are restyled with an accent spine on the active row, larger repo avatars, and an even column of status dots.

The Library is now a single master–detail view: a resizable, collapsible doc list beside an inline detail pane, so opening a document keeps your list scroll and filters instead of swapping pages. It adds a project switcher, an inline filter box, type tabs, docs grouped by type, a per-field-editable frontmatter card, a Narrow/Wide width toggle, and a “View on GitHub” link for the open doc. Switching documents now always seeds a fresh editor buffer, fixing a case where one doc's unsaved edits could be saved over another.

Light theme: the pipeline-stage badges, doc-type chips, diff add/delete colors, knowledge-graph nodes, and live-activity dots now deepen to legible tints on the cream surface instead of washing out, while the dark themes are left visually unchanged.

Question prompts now offer a custom “Other…” free-text answer when none of the preset options fit — for a single-select question the typed text and a preset pick are mutually exclusive, for multi-select the text is appended after the picked options, and pressing Enter advances or submits.

Fixed sessions that could wedge forever as “working” when you hit Stop or changed the permission mode while the agent was parked on a permission prompt or question. Stop now declines the prompt and settles the session to idle, and changing the permission level clears the card, restarts into the new mode, and flushes any queued messages.

Fixed the undersized, blurry Windows app icon by regenerating it with a full set of resolutions (16–256px) from a dedicated full-bleed source, so the taskbar, Alt-Tab, Start menu, and large-icon shell views all render sharp.

versions.summary: Start workstreams from existing branches or in-place, pin worktrees, attach PRs, and Escape-to-close.
notes: New workstreams can now start three ways: an isolated new branch in its own worktree (the default), an existing local branch checked out into its own worktree, or in-place — switching the project's own checkout onto a branch with no separate worktree. The New Workstream dialog replaces the base-branch dropdown with a searchable branch picker, and in-place rows carry a “no worktree” badge in the sidebar and board. Archive, restore, and delete never move, re-link, or remove a branch or repo the app didn't create.

Attach a specific open PR to a workstream by number, overriding branch-name detection for status, preview, and merge — handy when a workstream's branch doesn't match its pull request. The new picker offers free-text search and a live preview of the number you enter.

Pin frequently used worktrees to a new “Pinned” section at the top of the project sidebar so they're reachable without expanding their project tree. Pin or unpin from a worktree row's context menu; pins persist per user and drop out automatically when a worktree is archived or deleted.

Press Escape to close the topmost open surface — a dialog, context menu, or the Settings page — through one shared handler stack, so a modal opened over a page closes first and the next Escape falls through to the page beneath. Escape still reaches the terminal or editor when nothing dismissible is open.

⌘W can no longer close the last window on macOS. The Close Window menu item — one key away from ⌘⇧W (Close Agent Tab) — has been removed, so a slipped shortcut can't shut the window out from under running sessions; ⌘Q and the red traffic-light button remain the deliberate exits.
The Ship / PR / Archive controls now stay pinned to the window's right edge and no longer shift when a diff sidebar opens.

versions.summary: An animated brand mark beside the working timer, plus terminal-toggle and repo-path placeholder fixes.
notes: A small Hyprlayer mark now animates beside the elapsed-time counter while a session is working — a calm, branded progress cue whose three stacked layers glow in a bottom→top wave. It renders static under reduced-motion.

The toolbar terminal button now toggles the terminal: clicking it opens or reveals a hidden terminal and hides a visible one, matching the ⌘` shortcut. The button shows active state and its label switches between “Open terminal” and “Close terminal”; hiding keeps the PTY running for a later reveal.
Fixed misleading placeholder text in the repo path input — it now reads /path/to/your/repo instead of /path/to/your/thoughts.

versions.summary: A broad performance pass: smoother live sessions, GPU terminal, snappier sidebar, faster startup.
notes: Live sessions are noticeably smoother — the transcript and markdown only re-render the one message that is actively streaming (settled messages are memoized), and the text reveal is throttled, so a busy turn no longer bogs down the whole conversation.

The terminal now renders on the GPU via WebGL for fast, crisp output, with the prompt opened at the true grid size so a wrapping line no longer corrupts the redraw; it falls back to the standard renderer automatically if the GPU context is lost. Terminals also open as a login shell, so they pick up your shell profile.

The sidebar stays responsive with many workstreams: git-status checks now run in parallel rather than one after another, and the active worktree refreshes the moment its files change on disk — no window focus required.

Lower background overhead — the PR watcher pauses while the window is unfocused (waking on refocus), and database and filesystem work moved off the UI’s async path, so the app stays responsive during heavy turns.
Faster startup: heavy screens such as the document editor and the terminal/project view now load on demand instead of all up front.

versions.summary: Archive cleanup and worktree pruning, Shift+Tab stage cycling, plus terminal, docs, and Commit fixes.
notes: Workstreams now strip git-ignored build output and dependencies when archived (seeded files like .env are kept), and a new Clean up… button on the Archive page bulk permanent-deletes archives — all of them, or only those older than 30/60/90 days.

Cycle an un-started agent tab through its pipeline stages (General → Research → Plan → Implement → Validate) with a configurable keybinding (default Shift+Tab); the stage locks once the session starts.
Fixed a blank terminal (blinking cursor, no output) when resuming a session after an app restart, caused by reusing a single-use Tauri channel across the attach-then-open path.
Agent-created plans, research, and handoffs written outside the thoughts roots (e.g. under ~/.claude/plans/) now open in the read-only preview instead of failing with “not indexed.”
The manual Commit button now hides while a workstream’s Ship turn is in flight so it can’t race the commit Ship makes itself, and reappears if the ship fails or new uncommitted changes land.
The in-app update check now runs every 3 hours instead of every 6, so new releases surface sooner.

versions.summary: Worktree-copy warning badges, cleaner workstream creation, and self-clearing background tasks.
notes: Projects whose configured worktree-copy files don't resolve against the checkout now show a yellow warning badge on their sidebar row; hover it to see the offending patterns and the suggested fix. The check re-runs on startup, when you change the copy list, and when the window regains focus — so correcting a file on disk and tabbing back clears the warning without a restart.

Creating a workstream now always dismisses the dialog and jumps straight to the new workstream. Seed-copy problems surface on the project's warning badge instead of reopening an empty New workstream prompt.

Background shell tasks no longer linger as a phantom "running" task: reading a task's output file directly — the common case where the agent consumes the output and the completion notification is suppressed — now ends its live tracking.

versions.summary: Shell-style prompt history, configurable per-repo worktree file seeding, and a wider chat area.
notes: Step through the prompts you've already submitted this session with Alt+Up / Alt+Down (remappable in Settings → Keyboard), recalling each one into the composer to edit and resend. A stacked-lines graphic in the agent pane's top-right corner visualizes the history — hover a line to preview a prompt, click to recall — and it's capped at the 15 most recent, current session only.

Configure files that every new worktree should start with: a Worktree Files card in Project Settings writes a copy list to a committable .hyprlayer/settings.toml, and creating a workstream seeds those files (literal paths or globs) from the main checkout into the fresh worktree. Seeding is best-effort — a listed file that's missing is noted, never fatal.
Scrolling up while a reply streams now releases the auto-scroll instead of yanking you back to the bottom, and the view re-locks with a smooth glide once you return to the end.
The chat content area is now wider — 90% of the pane, up from 80% — and switching to a workstream drops the cursor straight into its composer so you can start typing without clicking first.

versions.summary: Compaction summaries fold into a collapsible divider, and finished background tasks now clear themselves.
notes: When a session compacts, the summary the agent writes afterward is now folded into the compaction divider as a collapsible panel — collapsed by default, with a chevron to expand it. Previously that block either flooded the transcript or was hidden entirely; now it sits inline on the divider, the same way a launched skill's body does.

Background shell tasks an agent starts and never checks again — fire-and-forget background commands — now disappear from the composer's background-task indicator as soon as they finish, instead of lingering as a phantom running task. The app acts on the agent's task-completion notification and clears the entry on any terminal status.

versions.summary: Live background shell tasks now surface in the composer toolbar with a status popover.
notes: When an agent leaves background shell tasks running — anything it started with a background Bash command — a pulsing terminal indicator now appears next to the context meter in the composer toolbar. Click it for a popover that lists each task with its label and a live elapsed timer, and click a row to jump the transcript to the call that spawned it.

Workstreams whose turn has finished but still have background shells running now show a distinct violet "background" activity state — on the workstream dot and in the Cmd+P search palette — so you can tell at a glance which sessions still have live processes.

versions.summary: Hyprlayer now runs on Windows (x64), with terminal and project fixes for the platform.
notes: Windows (x64) is now a supported platform: Hyprlayer ships a native Windows installer alongside the macOS (Apple Silicon) build, with the same in-app auto-updates — install it once and future versions arrive through the Update pill.

A set of Windows-specific fixes make agent sessions work end to end: the terminal now closes cleanly when its shell exits, project paths and the default shell (PowerShell) are detected correctly, and the app reliably locates its bundled CLI binary so agents launch as expected.

versions.summary: A guided first-run setup wizard, plus a header breadcrumb alignment fix.
notes: On first launch — or whenever your config is missing — Hyprlayer now opens a three-step setup wizard: enter your name, configure your AI CLI tool inline in an embedded terminal, and connect a thoughts repo by cloning one, picking a folder on disk, or creating a fresh one. You can re-run it anytime from Settings, which also gains an AI tool card showing your CLI's status with one-click reconfigure.

Fixed the header breadcrumb sliding under the window controls when the sidebar collapses — its inset is now derived from the actual left-cluster layout (and the number of visible controls) instead of a hard-coded macOS value, so it aligns correctly on both macOS and Linux.

versions.summary: Keyboard tab cycling, a Content Security Policy, plus terminal, docs, and commit-button fixes.
notes: Cycle through a pane's agent tabs from the keyboard — Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab move forward and back (Ctrl+PageUp / Ctrl+PageDown on Windows and Linux), wrapping at the ends and focusing the agent's composer.
Fixed a freshly opened integrated terminal that could stall at 80×24 — showing the full grid but acting hung — until you reattached; it now fits its pane on open.
Added a Content Security Policy to the desktop app, tightening what the in-app webview is allowed to load.
Commit and Ship buttons now read the live worktree git status, so they stay in lockstep with the Changes panel instead of lingering after you commit from the integrated terminal.
Fixed the attachment picker modal so it sizes correctly instead of overflowing, and long document lists now scroll inside it.
Library and workstream document lookups now match on the sanitized thoughts project key, so docs resolve even when a project's display name differs from its thoughts key.

versions.summary: Integrated terminal, a project board view, and a global Cmd+P search palette.
notes: Open an integrated terminal in the right dock — ⌘` toggles it open, revealed, or hidden. It runs your shell in the workstream's worktree, matches the active theme, remembers its font size (zoom in/out/reset), and keeps the session alive while hidden; shells are torn down only on tab close, workstream archive, or app exit.
Opening a project with no workstream selected now shows a dashboard board — every workstream as a card with its git status and stage — instead of auto-opening the last-used chat.
Press Cmd+P to open a global search palette that fuzzy-matches across all workstreams, live agents, library docs, and worktree files, and jumps straight to whatever you pick.

Docs that an agent writes through a worktree's thoughts/ symlink now resolve to the real file, so opening, saving, revealing, or editing their frontmatter from the library works instead of missing the index.

versions.summary: Archive workspaces non-destructively, OS toasts when agents need attention, and attachment cards for @file.
notes: Archive a workstream from the sidebar to put it on ice without losing the worktree or branch — unarchive or permanently delete it later from the new Archive view.
When an agent transitions to needs-you while the window is unfocused or you're on another tab, a native OS toast fires; clicking it within 15 seconds jumps to that workstream.

Picking a file from the @file dropdown now stages it as an attachment card instead of leaving a raw path in the prompt, and /commands fire on any whitespace-delimited token rather than only at the start of the message.
At 60% context usage a banner suggests running /create_handoff; once the doc is written it attaches as a tab chip and the Eraser button glows amber so Clear & resume picks up where you left off.
Syntax token colors in fenced code blocks now draw from each theme's own palette rather than bleeding Dark+ defaults onto light, claude, cobalt, matrix, and solarized surfaces.

versions.summary: Rewind a conversation to an earlier user message and re-send an edited prompt.
notes: Hover any of your messages in the transcript to reveal a Rewind action that truncates the conversation back to that turn, repopulates the composer with the original prompt for editing, and resumes from the truncated state.
User turns now show a relative timestamp and a copy-prompt button on the same hover toolbar.

versions.summary: Syntax-highlighted code blocks in chat and library markdown.
notes: Fenced code blocks in assistant messages and library docs now render with Shiki syntax highlighting that tracks the active theme.
Highlighting waits for streaming to settle, so messages render plain monospace while they stream and recolor once complete.

versions.summary: Remove project dialog, compact-boundary markers in the transcript, and a stop button that always stops.
notes: Remove a project from the sidebar with a new Remove dialog — optionally delete its directory from disk.
The transcript now shows a labelled divider when a conversation is compacted, so the pause is visible instead of looking like a hang.
The Stop button now hard-kills wedged turns after a short grace window, so a frozen turn can always be stopped.
The Open-in menu now puts your default editor first, and app icons match the surrounding icon weight.
Archiving a workstream whose worktree had become a husk (directory present, .git gone) no longer hangs.

versions.summary: Customizable keyboard shortcuts, per-provider model defaults, and smarter context-doc suggestions.
notes: Set your own keyboard shortcuts for common actions in Settings → Keyboard.
New sessions can default to a chosen model per provider.
Each pane suggests the most relevant context doc (research or plan) for its stage.
The CI Checks panel now flags merge conflicts that block merging.

versions.summary: Live markdown while messages stream, and fixed clipped composer picker dropdowns.
notes: Assistant messages now render markdown live as they stream, instead of showing raw text until the message completes.
The composer mode and model pickers open their dropdowns again — the toolbar overflow fix no longer clips them.

versions.summary: Choose the base branch when creating a workstream.
notes: The New workstream dialog now has a base-branch picker, defaulting to the repo's detected default branch.
Base a workstream off a release line or feature branch instead of always branching from main.

versions.summary: Workstream activity dots, in-place project imports, and split-pane drop and composer toolbar fixes.
notes: Add an existing project from disk in place instead of re-cloning it.
Workstream cards show activity indicator dots while a session is working.
Drag-and-drop now targets the pane under the cursor in a split session.
Composer toolbar collapses to icons on real overflow, never bleeding past the pane edge.

versions.summary: Composer /skill and @file autocomplete, a Commit action, clear-context, and skill-display fixes.

Commit a worktree without shipping, plus push-based PR status sync and check links.
Clear a session to start a fresh conversation, and run more agents concurrently.
Skill activity now shows the skill name and folds its instructions into one row.

versions.summary: Configurable git settings, an Open-in-editor menu, and resizable, responsive layout polish.
notes: Configure branch-name prefix, automerge, archive-on-merge, and delete-branch-on-archive in a redesigned Settings page.
Open the active worktree in any installed editor, terminal, or file manager from the header.
Resizable diff sidebar, a composer that adapts to narrow panes, and toggleable nav icons.

versions.summary: Ship PRs in-app with CI tracking and merge, per-session permission modes, and UI polish.
notes: Ship a workstream to a GitHub pull request from the header, then track CI checks, merge, and archive.
Choose a permission mode per session — Auto, Ask each time, Accept edits, Plan only, or Bypass.
Polished update notifier with release notes, symmetric sidebars, and a primary-button hover fix.

Click a change to open a rich unified or side-by-side diff.
